text:
alex: FYI saw a 3x latency spike for the eu-west GPU pool during the 02:00 deploy window. Looks correlated with a scale-to-zero cycle for the prewarm pool. Anyone else see this? :thinking:

jing: saw it too. metric spike for 'request_wait_time' around 02:03-02:07. heatmap shows warm-pool size dropped to 0 for ~30s before new nodes came up.

marie: was the warm-pool configured with snooze mode? I thought we had a 1-min cooldown.

kevin: config in cluster-autoscaler was changed last week to be more aggressive: --scale-down-unneeded-time=1m and --max-empty-bulk-delete=10. That made warm pools drain faster.

alex: here's the sequence I pulled from logs:
```
02:00:01  prewarm: scale-down triggered for gpu-prewarm-np size=3 -> 0
02:02:55  request spike hits; no prewarmed nodes available
02:03:10  k8s: launching new node(s) (on-demand fallback)
02:04:05  serving restored; latency back to baseline
```

sahil: are the scale-up instances always on-demand? If we fall back to on-demand there's a 30-60s boot penalty. For eu-west we prefer reserved/dedicated as fallback.

jing: good call. For cost reasons CA zeros empty pools to save OPEX, but for GPUs the coldstart cost is user-visible. we used to keep 1 node as "snooze-reserve" in the dedicated pools.

marie: small experiments: 1) add a min-size=1 to the gpu-prewarm node pool 2) bump cooldown to 5m 3) use instance-templates with a faster image init (pre-baked containerd+drivers). Which should we try first?

kevin: i'd start with min-size=1 on the warm pool. Lowest friction. Also we can mark pods as critical so CA won't evict them, or use the new WarmPool feature (if supported).

alex: agree. I'll open a quick patch. Proposed kubectl patch:
```
kubectl patch nodepool gpu-prewarm -p '{"spec": {"minSize": 1, "autoScale": {"enabled": true}}}'
```

sahil: also add an annotation so scheduler prefers reserved instances: `redwood/instance-class=reserved`. That should route cold starts to cheaper reserved capacity first.

ops-bot: Deploy Bot: patch applied to cluster-eu-west by alex at 1794501400.

jing: after patch applied i still see a small blip but warm-pool stayed at 1. latency now only 10-15% above baseline vs 3x before. looks promising.

marie: follow-up: we should evaluate two longer-term changes: - integrate a light-weight "warm agent" that stays in memory (reduces container startup) - experiment with tiny pinned forever instance (g4dn.xlarge-like) in each region. both give different cost/latency tradeoffs.

kevin: can we get a simple cost delta for keeping 1 min-sized reserved node vs the occasional on-demand spin? crunch numbers for eu-west 24x7 vs burst frequency.

alex: i'll throw numbers into a quick spreadsheet and post results. if we see sustained bursts we can start using a short-lived burst pool instead of full min-size.

sahil: one last note — check driver robustness when nodes are prewarmed and then sit idle for hours. we had a case where GPU driver lost persistence after kernel updates. consider periodic health check that recreates idle prewarm pods weekly.

alex: good call. i'll add a cron job to restart prewarm pods every 24h and alert if restart rate > 1 in 24h.

ops-bot: Incident Tracker: created ticket INF-3472 "eu-west prewarm coldstart spike" assigned to alex, jing, kevin.

alex: thanks everyone. i'll monitor next 3 deploy windows and report back. :thumbsup:
